newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine '96 refined sugar output seen 3.2 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine '96 refined sugar output seen 3.2 mln T.

text.p: Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Anatoly Khorishko on Wednesday predicted that Ukraine's refined sugar output from its 1996 beet crop would be 3.2 million tonnes.

"We are expecting to gather 26 million tonnes of sugar beets this year and to refine 3.2 million tonnes of sugar," he told a news conference, repeating earlier forecasts of the sugar beet harvest. Ukraine produced 3.485 million tonnes of refined sugar last year.
Khorishko blamed poor weather at the start of summer and heavy rains in September for the poor sugar beet harvest outlook.
Last year Ukraine harvested 30 million tonnes of beets.
Khorishko said warm weather conditions for October meant that some losses could be stemmed.
The sugar beet harvest is 25 percent complete.
"We will continue to export Ukrainian sugar," Khorishko said. "Previously we exported about two million tonnes, but exports will be less in 1997."
Government forecasts earlier this year had put 1996 refined sugar exports at 1.7 million tonnes.
More than 100 Ukrainian refineries have started processing beets and more than 150,000 tonnes of sugar have been produced.
